title: Melbourne / Naarm Knowledge Seed R1
geography: Greater Melbourne and common day-trip regions
source_policy: Grade A government, public museum, library, cultural institution or destination authority sources. Dynamic visitor details require runtime recheck.
cultural_safety: First Peoples material requires Traditional Owner authority, pronunciation review and cultural approval before public narration.

nodes.claim: Birrarung Marr and its artworks interpret First Peoples connections to the river; the City walk explains Birrarung as river of mists and marr as edge.
Eastern Hill was an important Eastern Kulin meeting and ceremonial landscape before and during early colonisation.
Melbourne's surveyed grid dates to 1837; its geometry overlaid existing Country and natural drainage, with Elizabeth Street following a former watercourse.
The 1850s gold rush rapidly expanded Victoria's population, trade and infrastructure while also intensifying exclusion and dispossession.
The 1854 census records a fast-growing and internationally born colonial population; birthplace categories must not be presented as ethnicity.
The Immigration Museum occupies the former Customs House, whose present building entered use in 1858 and was completed in 1876.
Chinese community life was established around Little Bourke Street by the mid-1850s; Num Pon Soon is among its key surviving community buildings.

source.org: City of Melbourne Libraries / Heritage Victoria
source.title: Kong Meng & Co. Warehouse and Num Pon Soon Society

nodes.claim: The site became a railway terminus in 1854; the present main station building was developed from the Fawcett and Ashworth design and completed in 1910.
Federation Square opened in 2002 above an engineered deck over railway lines and platforms.
ACMI opened to the public at Federation Square in 2002 and focuses on moving-image culture.
Founded in 1861, the NGV operates NGV International and The Ian Potter Centre: NGV Australia.
The Melbourne Public Library opened in 1856; the domed La Trobe Reading Room opened in 1913.
The gaol's first cell block opened in 1845 and later became deeply associated with colonial justice and the gold-rush city's growth.
Construction began in 1856; the building served as the Commonwealth Parliament's home from 1901 to 1927 and its original design remains incomplete.
Built for the 1880 Melbourne International Exhibition, it hosted the opening of the first Commonwealth Parliament in 1901 and became World Heritage listed in 2004.
The Shrine opened in 1934; it is Victoria's principal memorial to Australian service and sacrifice in war and peacekeeping.
Established in 1846, Melbourne Gardens covers 38 hectares and supports botanical collections, research and conservation.
Queen Victoria Market is a heritage-listed open-air market and a major continuing small-business and food precinct.
The official lanes and arcades walk is about 2.4 km and two hours, linking central laneways, arcades, street art and hospitality.
The official street-art walk is about 3 km and two hours; artworks are deliberately treated as changeable rather than permanent facts.
The official central gardens walk is about 4.2 km and two hours, linking major nineteenth-century parks and gardens.
The official Yarra discovery walk follows roughly 2 km of waterfront and interprets history, public art and contemporary river life.
The official architecture walk links gold-rush-era facades, Gothic Revival, Art Deco and modern civic architecture over about 4.3 km.
St Kilda's foreshore supports walking, cycling and bay views between the pier and southern viewing areas.
St Kilda, Brighton and Williamstown form a useful bay-beach theme, but are not a single continuous walking route.
Williamstown developed from 1837 as Melbourne's first port and retains strong maritime and bay-view associations.
Yarra Bend is Melbourne's largest natural bushland park, with river walks, Dights Falls and a flying-fox colony.
Albert Park is an inner-city lake landscape used for walking, cycling, recreation and skyline views.
Its salt lake can appear pink only under suitable warm, dry and saline conditions; the colour must never be promised.
The park's basalt columns formed as lava cooled more than one million years ago; access includes a steep walking route.
The ranges combine mountain-ash forest, fern gullies, waterfalls and recreation areas roughly an hour from central Melbourne.
The Yarra Ranges route combines cool forest, Black Spur and Mount Donna Buang viewpoints; road and snow conditions are dynamic.
The You Yangs are granite peaks rising from surrounding plains; Flinders Peak includes a substantial stair climb and broad views.
The peninsula combines sheltered bay shores, exposed Bass Strait coast, national parks and maritime landscapes.
The 26 km trail connects Dromana and Cape Schanck through Arthurs Seat and Mornington Peninsula parklands; it requires fitness planning.
The 1859 lighthouse landscape includes coastal geology and boardwalk viewpoints; closures and control operations require live checks.
Point Nepean combines Port Phillip and Bass Strait views with quarantine and military heritage at the peninsula's western end.
Visit Victoria's touring route links Melbourne, San Remo, Cowes and the Penguin Parade; listed duration is driving time, not total touring time.
The official multi-day route links Melbourne, Torquay, Apollo Bay, the Twelve Apostles, Port Campbell and Port Fairy before returning inland.
